Direct coordination by the Architect is only the developer-chosen exception. When another agent started you, report to that agent's role with its task references, unless the Architect instructs the reporting-recipient change below.

Preserve stable requirement/finding IDs and distinguish implementation, review, curation and publication status. Direct leaf repair-loop handovers run as `../operations/coordination.md` states.

passages.beforeText: Decide the order of your leaves, agent starts and replacements, operational problems, ordinary requirement interpretation within the intended promise, checks before and after a landing, and paired closeout and integration within delegated authority. Review rounds, memory passes and relay limits follow `../operations/coordination.md`. Accepting a verdict for the gate stays yours. Assign a check or investigation that belongs to no leaf to an Investigator on your own sprint and master. Send the scoped concern as your first `role_message` on `agents-remember-task` to its returned agent ID; never select a leaf for this role.
passages.afterText: Decide the order of your leaves, agent starts and replacements, operational problems, ordinary requirement interpretation within the intended promise, checks before and after a landing, and paired closeout and integration within delegated authority. Accepting a verdict for the gate stays yours. The task's construction is yours: step order, evidence form, which existing test or command shows a thing, one rerun on the same operands after a harness, loader or capture fault, and sandbox- or scratch-only instruments that change no product source; a second failure of one cause goes up with what was tried. passages.duty: Escalate an hour-long item or second repair round/freeze with hours and proposal
passages.beforeText: When another agent started you, message your parent or the instructed reporting recipient only for a developer decision: new or dropped scope or a change to a requirement's promise; something only the developer can do or approve; an override of a role default; or a blocker that none of your own decisions can remove. Send these with `role_message` on `agents-remember-task` to the parent agent ID in your handover, or to the instructed reporting-recipient ID recorded in your report. When the Orchestrator owns coordination, do not bypass it to the Architect. Forward only questions requiring the developer and permission notices as stated below; send no other role messages or landing notices. Ordinary requirement readings and operational rulings stay with you; keep the work going. Send one further message with the path of your report, addressed to the parent's role with its task references, when the whole assignment is finished or cannot be finished. Send no other messages to that recipient.
passages.afterText: When another agent started you, message your parent or the instructed reporting recipient only for a developer decision: new or dropped scope or a change to a requirement's promise; something only the developer can do or approve; an override of a role default; a small item that has cost about an hour, or a second repair round or freeze, with its hours and a proposal; or a blocker that none of your own decisions can remove. passages.duty: Direct pending handover occasion plus first-message Reviewer intake for leaf and integration/master-exit
passages.beforeText: The Manager receives the Worker’s freeze notice to start the Reviewer and the Reviewer’s code-PASS notice to start the Curator, plus only what `../roles/manager.md` lists for the Manager. It supplies the occasion for the sender to retry a pending hand-over, without relaying contents or asking for developer confirmation of that occasion. Read reports and task records for routine state and record which seat holds each next step and since when. Starts refused `intent-review-open` wait for architect's `go`; never retry.
passages.afterText:
The Manager receives the Worker’s freeze notice to start the Reviewer and the Reviewer’s code-PASS notice to start the Curator, plus only what `../roles/manager.md` lists for the Manager. For a pending hand-over, the Manager gives the sender the occasion to retry and relays no contents. Do not ask the developer to confirm that occasion. Read reports and task records for routine state and record which seat holds each next step and since when. Starts refused `intent-review-open` wait for architect's `go`; never retry.

After the individual `role_start` on `agents-remember-task`, send the leaf Reviewer's intake as your first `role_message` to the returned agent ID: review mode, canonical task and review purpose, seam, requirement set (IDs, versions, packets, durable corpus ruling), bound catalogs and resolved `system/tools.md`. Candidate identity and attempt records arrive with the Worker's freeze; the Reviewer inspects nothing before its intake.

For integration or master-exit, start the Reviewer on the master task data's acceptance and delivery-proof leaf, with its sprint and master; if none is named, ask the architect. Send the intake above, adding candidate identity and attempt records, as your first `role_message` on `agents-remember-task` to the returned agent ID.

dutyWordEvidence.text:
Keep your role fixed, refuse another role's brief and report the mismatch to your parent; direct coordination grants no other role (AU1.1, AU2.8, AU3.1, AU3.2)
Architect, Orchestrator, Manager: Start each role once with its exact task selection and request ID, reconcile uncertainty with that ID, and report a refusal without another-tool fallback (AU4.1, AU5.5)
Architect, Orchestrator, Manager: Settings supply harness, model and effort unless overridden, and starts carry no mode; start Worker, then Reviewer when ready, then Curator after code PASS (AU4.1)
Architect, Orchestrator, Manager: After an override start, check and set the seat’s mode and features, recording the product defect rather than removing overrides (AU4.2)
Architect, Orchestrator, Manager: Resolve a developer-declared task-seat takeover, start that canonical role rather than become it, and report its dashboard location (AU5.1, AU5.2, AU5.3, AU5.4)
Escalate high-impact truth questions immediately; decide and log presentation choices yourself (AU6.2)
Read the active queue before treating clarification as current or future work, expose in-scope changes, record future work durably, and ask your parent when the fit is unclear (AU7.1, AU7.2, AU7.3, AU7.4)
Architect, Orchestrator, Manager: Preview and execute accepted-series transactions within delegated authority; preserve distinct gate deciders, human-pinned approvals and developer decisions (AU8.1, AU8.2)
Architect: Present developer questions individually, record and relay the actual ruling, and ask the sender once when the item is underspecified (AU9.3, AU9.4)
Create no watcher, poll or timer loop; answer a waking message before ending the turn (AU10.2)
Collect helpers and continue ordinary work, preserving native within-turn collection (AU10.3)
On the declared ACP wait path, end with `WAITING FOR SUBAGENTS:`, report each helper in your own chat, collect finished work and declare again or continue, without parent progress messages or another wake mechanism (AU10.3)
Change instruction text through a task, never by rewriting a role file to settle disagreement (AU11.1)
Architect, Orchestrator, Manager, Worker, Curator, Reviewer: Publish only authorized code and memory, report focused checks truthfully, and carry curation's complete memory-quality result without inventing automatic full-suite or review work (AU11.3)
Architect, Orchestrator, Manager: Publishing—push to the sprint line, pull requests and release—belongs to the developer unless explicitly delegated (AU11.4)
A claim about all members checks the complete claimed population; absence searches the relevant tree completely (IN1.2)
Record covered scope and truncation, checks run and left out, and same-cause base evidence by message and subtest before calling a failure pre-existing (IN1.2)
Put decisions and rulings on their durable surface, send developer questions through the named parent, and continue independent work; without a parent ask in your own chat (IN2.1, IN2.3, IN2.4, IN4.2, AU9.2)
Parallelize independent work by default with named reasons for sequencing, without an invented concurrency cap; serial landing order remains (IN3.1, IN3.3)
Name a gate, one-writer dependency, ruling or harness without helpers for sequencing; only the developer authorizes a concurrency limit (IN3.2)
Guards need observed recurring cause and developer acceptance (IN3.4)
Architect, Investigator: Before releasing a requirement, disclose every added refusal, limit or narrowing beyond the developer's words and obtain the developer's yes (IN3.4)
Full inputs and pages have no invented count cap (IN3.4)
Architect, Orchestrator, Designer, Strategist: Planning and design create no branch, worktree or commit (IN5.2)
Architect, Orchestrator, Manager, Worker, Bootstrap: Make code changes under an approved task, using the light-task workflow for small work rather than building from chat (IN5.5)
Fulfil the task and fill small unambiguous blanks; escalate a plan delta rather than reshape your assignment (IN6.1, IN6.2)
Orchestrator, Manager, Worker: Keep the spirit test with the Orchestrator, never move it down to Managers or Workers (IN6.3)
Architect, Orchestrator, Manager, Designer, Strategist, Bootstrap: Apply the task-collaboration doctrine when scoping, without paraphrasing it (IN8.1)
Read the resolved memory-layer tools, coding and publication instructions rather than inventing commands (IN8.3)
Instructions and requirements point to the repository’s own guideline files and never restate their content (IN8.5)
Design rules belong to repository `system/design-guidelines.md`, never role text or code defaults; shipped designs are examples and AR’s look is never imposed (IN8.6)
Architect, Orchestrator, Manager, Worker, Investigator: During provider degradation, continue valid native reads, report blockers, start no providers, and leave state changes to the owning Worker under explicit authority (LF2.2, LF2.3, LF2.4)
Architect: Propose a strategist pre-run; run it only after developer approval (LO5.1)
Architect: Before task topology, obtain developer approval for versioned requirement packets on the canonical template, with required diagrams; revise and rebrief affected leaves when intent changes (LO6.2, LO6.3)
Architect, Orchestrator, Manager, Worker: Before dispatch, bind the primary ID, version, packet and corpus ruling, labeling dependency and preservation context separately (AC2.1)
Architect, Orchestrator, Manager: Validate the exact handoff artifact, candidate and evidence before advancing a gate; act on missing or stale artifacts (AC0.3, AC0.4)
Worker, Reviewer, Curator: Check the exact object and requested stretch before taking a peer handover (AC0.3)
Completion is not acceptance; write the artifact before handing over and message its waiting recipient; add no model-written completion row or another seat's runtime identity (AC0.1, AC0.5, AC1.9)
Worker: Deliver one primary acceptance block with status, delivery rationale and anchors, verification rationale naming the caught failure, and exact command/results; explain blocked or approved changes with their developer ruling (AC2.2, AC2.3, AC2.4, AC2.5, AC2.6, AC2.7, AC2.8, AC2.9)
Reviewer: Inspect the exact primary revision and artifacts independently; reject missing or wrong evidence, and retain BLOCK for a truthful but undelivered blocked requirement (AC2.10)
Worker: Advance attempts only at review handoff; record internal reruns separately with candidate, command, result, cause, repair and next proof (AC3.2, AC3.3)
Worker: Validate and append immutable candidate-bound journal records before review handoff; preserve and void malformed unsent rows without consuming an ID, and let the Reviewer reject already-handed-off rows (AC3.4, AC3.5)
Worker, Reviewer: Repair through a successor citing predecessor and sealed findings; never reopen closed attempts, and send outside-list changes through the parent without resetting review (AC3.7)
Manager: Keep a rebuildable journal summary that never becomes authority or blocks work (AC4.1)
Worker, Reviewer: Give retained evidence either contract identity, owner, executable node and consumers, or expiry, executable removal/replacement, owner and compatibility consequence; missing catalog metadata is implementation work, independent of requirement acceptance (AC5.1, AC5.2, AC5.3, AC5.4, AC5.5)
